question: Find the value of x satisfying: 5(5x² − 6) − 5(5x² + 2x − 4) = 20
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Divide the entire equation by 5 to simplify calculations directly.

⇒ (5x² − 6) − (5x² + 2x − 4) = 4

Notice that the 5x² terms perfectly cancel each other out.

⇒ −6 − 2x + 4 = 4

⇒ −2x − 2 = 4 ⇒ −2x = 6 ⇒ x = −3

**∴ The correct answer is -3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

5(5x² − 6) − 5(5x² + 2x − 4) = 20

**Calculation:**

Expand the brackets by multiplying 5 with each term:

⇒ (25x² − 30) − (25x² + 10x − 20) = 20

Carefully apply the negative sign to every term inside the second bracket:

⇒ 25x² − 30 − 25x² − 10x + 20 = 20

Cancel out the 25x² terms:

⇒ −10x − 10 = 20

⇒ −10x = 30

⇒ x = 30 ÷ (−10)

⇒ x = −3

**∴ The correct answer is -3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

Always follow the order of Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction. When opening brackets with a negative sign outside, you must invert the sign of every single term inside.

Linear Equations

Even if an equation initially contains quadratic terms (x²), they may cancel out to form a simple linear equation of the form ax + b = 0, which always has a single solution given by x = −b/a.
